To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the designer drugs MDA, MDMA and MDE are metabolized in the liver to the catechol derivatives 3,4-methylenedi-oxyamphetamine (MDAH), 3,4- methylenediooxymethamphetamine (PMAH), and 3,4 methylenediooxyethylamphetamine (MDEH), which are conjugated with sulfate or glucuronide.

the designer drug amphetamine derivatives MDA, MDMA and MBDA are metabolized by CYP2A2/4 and CYP1A1/2 to their corresponding catechol derivatives, which are further metabolized by catechol- O-methyltransferase and glucuronidation to their corresponding O-methoxy derivatives.
the main metabolites of amphetamine-derived 'Ecstasy' designer drugs are demethylated and dealkylated derivatives.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolism of amphetamine-derived drugs in humans is not only catalyzed by COMT and the cytochrome P450 system, but also by other enzymes and pathways.
the metabolism of the amphetamine-derived designer drug derivatives is mainly catalyzed in the liver by CYP1, 2 and 3 enzymes, and to a lesser degree by COMT and other enzymes.
the metabolism of amphetamine-derived drugs is complex, but can be predicted based on the metabolism of the parent compound amphetamine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the designer drugs MDA, MDMA and MBDA are metabolized in humans and rats in a similar way as the prototype amphetamine.
the designer drug amphetamine derivatives are mainly metabolized by CYP2, but also by other CYP isoforms, and that the metabolite pattern in humans differs from the one in rats.
the toxicokinetic and analytical toxicological data are in agreement with the postulated metabolic pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the toxicology of amphetamines is very complex and that the toxicological analysis should not be restricted to the detection of amphetamine itself, but that the analysis should be extended to the phase I and phase II metabolites.
there are no specific metabolites that could be used to distinguish among these drugs and their metabolites.

the metabolism and excretion of amphetamine-derived drugs can be predicted based on their structural similarity to the parent compound amphetamine and that these predictions can be confirmed using in vitro systems.
